comments.author: Alexander Terp
comments.body:
Second sighting, on 0.8.1, in window 3742. Stale for 75 minutes, and this time `supervise` logged nothing at all - not even the `tunnel.down` / `tunnel.reopened` pair that preceded the 40-minute silence above.

From `muster-2026-09-14_08-43-25-3742.jsonl`:

    13:44:22.094Z  tunnel.reopened           the forwarded socket is bound and a command came back
    14:01:12.278Z  mirror.resnapshot.failed  timed out
    14:01:24.866Z  mirror.resnapshot.failed  unreachable (Connection refused (os error 61))
    (no tunnel event after 13:44:22Z)

`ps -o lstart,ppid` puts the takeover inside one second:

    14:01:12Z  ssh -S ...-devenv.ctl -o BatchMode=yes aterp-chco   pid 26765, ppid 26764 (a bridge)
    14:01:13Z  ssh: ...-devenv.ctl [mux]                           pid 26794, ppid 1

The master Muster spawned died, and a bridge's client had the path back before the next `HEALTH_POLL`. The supervisor never saw an unanswered check, so there is no `tunnel.down` to find this time.

## What the person at the keyboard got

Nothing. `session.rs:869` raises the daemon-unreachable warning from `TunnelState::Unreachable`, and `supervise` only reports that state after `PATIENCE` consecutive `tunnel.down`. No `tunnel.down`, so no problem, and no remedy offered - while `backend.stale` was logged 3244 times and the mirror took `ECONNREFUSED` every few seconds. The window's own signal was there and unused, which is the third fix above.

Zoom and focus surfaced it again, and the attempts are in the log:

    15:04:43Z  FocusPane p22msx4e35  refused: unreachable (Connection refused (os error 61))
    15:04:44Z  ZoomPane  p22msx4e35  refused  (three times)
    15:05:04Z  FocusPane p22my9c0er  refused

32 `core.refused` in all, over 40 seconds of trying. The CRAB tab would not unzoom and tab 1 would not take the keyboard.

## A recovery that costs no bridge

`kill` on the master reproduced the takeover exactly as `-O exit` did above: a new `[mux]` and five respawned bridges within the same second, no `tunnel.down`. Re-binding the forward on the bridge's master instead leaves every channel up:

    rm /var/.../muster-3742-devenv.sock
    ssh -O forward \
        -L /var/.../muster-3742-devenv.sock:/home/.config/herdr/sessions/muster/herdr.sock \
        -S /var/.../muster-3742-devenv.ctl aterp-chco

`connected` on the next resnapshot, and the requests that had been refused landed: tab 1 came back with its four-pane tree, CRAB unzoomed. Worth having for somebody mid-session, since moving the control path aside costs every bridge its channel. It unblocks rather than fixes - Muster is left supervising a master it did not spawn, with no `-L` of its own and `ControlPersist 10m`.

creator: Alexander Terp
description:
The devenv daemon sat `stale (Connection refused (os error 61))` for 40 minutes in window 87686 on 0.7.0, while `ssh -O check` on its control path answered `Master running` throughout. `supervise` logged nothing in those 40 minutes, because the question it asks - does a master answer the control path - was true. The master answering was not Muster's: it was a pane bridge's ssh, promoted to master by the user's `ControlMaster auto`, carrying no `-L` forward.

`a_2J1KZ9FbM` pinned `ControlPersist=no` and moved the health question off a pid and onto the control path. Its comment reads "asking the path as well means no future ssh can put the bug back". Any ssh with `ControlMaster auto` can put it back, Muster's own included.

A stale devenv is easy to miss, because every pane keeps its last frame. What surfaced it was zoom: tab 1 was zoomed and would not unzoom, tab 2 was not zoomed and would not zoom. Zoom is daemon truth, so both directions need a request that lands, and `muster zoom` answered `the daemon did not make that change: unreachable (Connection refused (os error 61))`.

## What was measured

From `muster-2026-09-09_13-10-46-87686.jsonl`:

    17:30:12.218Z  tunnel.down       `-O check` did not answer within 2s
    17:30:12.334Z  tunnel.master_ended  the master left when the control path asked it to
    17:30:13.312Z  tunnel.reopened   the forwarded socket is bound and a command came back
    17:31:00.135Z  mirror.resnapshot.failed  unreachable (Connection refused (os error 61))
    (no tunnel event for the next 40 minutes)

At 18:03Z, with the window still stale:

    ssh -O check on muster-87686-devenv.ctl  -> Master running (pid=67431)
    ps -o lstart -p 67431                    -> 17:30:51Z, 38s after the reopen above
    lsof -U | rg muster-87686-devenv.sock    -> nothing bound to it
    connect(muster-87686-devenv.sock)        -> ECONNREFUSED

So Muster's master died within 38 seconds of being confirmed, 67431 took the control path over, and the forwarded socket file it left behind refuses every connection. `-O check` answers, `confirm` would pass, and nothing dials the socket that every mirror request uses.

## The takeover

A bridge's command line, from `ps`:

    ssh -S /var/.../muster-87686-devenv.ctl -o BatchMode=yes aterp-chco \
        sh -c '... herdr terminal session control w6:pQ --cols 189 --rows 61 --takeover'

No `ControlMaster` on it, so `~/.ssh/config` decides, and `Host aterp-chco` says `ControlMaster auto` with `ControlPersist 10m`. Under `auto`, a client that finds nothing answering its `-S` path becomes the master for that path - and this path is Muster's own. It forwards nothing, because the `-L` exists only in `master_arguments`, and it persists ten minutes past its last session.

Three sites run ssh at that path with no `ControlMaster` pinned:

- `crates/muster-bridge/src/main.rs:283` - the pane bridge, one per pane, respawned whenever a channel dies. Ten panes on a devenv is ten clients racing to bind the moment a master dies.
- `crates/muster-ssh/src/remote.rs:52` - `Remote::run`, which is what `confirm` sends its `true` over. With `auto`, that call can create the master it is checking for, so a reopen can be confirmed by its own check.
- `crates/muster-ssh/src/tunnel.rs:587` - `remote_environment`, which passes no `-S` and so can only reuse the user's own `ControlPath`. Not a route into this bug.

## Killing the master does not recover it

Asked directly, at 18:09Z:

    ssh -S muster-87686-devenv.ctl -O exit aterp-chco   -> Exit request sent
    new [mux] process at 13:09:06 local, pid 10150      <- a bridge, same second
    bridge processes respawned at 13:09:15
    daemon state, polled for 8s                         -> stale, all 8 polls

No `tunnel.down` was logged. Ending the master kills every bridge channel riding it, all of those bridges respawn immediately, and one of them binds the control path inside a single `HEALTH_POLL`. The supervisor never sees an unanswered check, so a person who works out what is wrong still cannot make the window fix itself.

## The recovery that worked

Move the control path aside rather than ending the master, so the bridges' sessions stay up and nothing respawns to race for it:

    mv muster-87686-devenv.ctl muster-87686-devenv.ctl.orphan

`-O check` failed on the next poll, `end_master` unlinked the stale forwarded socket, `spawn` brought up Muster's own master with the `-L` (pid 12259), `confirm` passed, and the mirror bootstrapped: `connected` within two seconds. One `muster zoom` then unzoomed tab 1. herdr's `session.json` had `zoomed: true` on tab 1 with the full eight-pane tree intact the whole time, so nothing was lost - the window just could not reach it.

The orphan master keeps running until its sessions end, and its own control path is now an unlinked inode.

## Fix

Pin `-o ControlMaster=no` at both `-S` sites, `main.rs:283` and `remote.rs:52`, beside the `BatchMode=yes` already there. Then only the `-M` process Muster spawned can hold that path, and `-O check` means what `supervise` assumes it means. `ControlPersist=no` belongs there too, so a client that somehow does become one cannot outlive its session by ten minutes.

Worth deciding alongside it, and this is the part that stops the class: `supervise` should ask the transport it actually depends on. The mirror gets `ECONNREFUSED` on the forwarded socket every few seconds while the supervisor calls the tunnel healthy, and a supervisor that dialed that socket would need no theory about who owns the control path. `a_2J1KZ9FbM` raised the same question ("whether `supervise` should trust the transport over the pid at all") and answered half of it by moving to the control path. The control path turned out to be somebody else's to answer.

Cheaper than either, and worth having regardless: nothing routes the mirror's own refusal back to the tunnel. A daemon that has been `stale` with a refused socket for more than a few seconds is grounds to rebuild the tunnel, and that signal already exists in the mirror.

## Why the suite missed it

The devenv container's ssh config has no `ControlMaster auto` - the same blind spot `a_2J1KZ9FbM` was measured against, one option along. And the takeover needs a bridge to dial the control path in a moment when no master answers, so a test has to kill Muster's master while panes are attached and then let the bridges respawn, with `ControlMaster auto` in the client config for the run.
title: 🔌 A pane bridge takes over the master, so -O check calls a forwardless tunnel healthy
